title: Power-Building Guide
subtitle: Strength-focused exercise choices and how the blocks fit together
summary: Notes to go with the two Power-Building programs: how the hypertrophy and strength blocks fit together, and the powerlifting accessory exercises that support the bench press, squat and deadlift.

sections.heading: The structure
body: The power-building plan has a mainly-hypertrophy block of 12 weeks (8, then 12, then 15 working sets, with the main lifts at 80%, 75% and 70% of your 1RM), followed by a mainly-strength block of 4 weeks (6-8 working sets in total) and a deload.
You must stick to the RIR and the percentages, otherwise you will get fatigued very quickly.

sections.heading: Between the blocks
body: For the accessory work in the strength block, repeat one of your favorite workouts from the 8 working set mesocycle.
Take a deload week after the strength block, or 2-3 weeks of almost no lifting. Then start again at the beginning of the hypertrophy block with your new %RM.

sections.heading: Volume management
body: If you do not think 5 sets of incline bench press is worth it when your maximum volume for that day on chest is 5, you can opt to do a lower version, for example 3 sets. Just stay with the given weight and RIR.

sections.heading: Bench press
body: Pin or board press: for lockout work.
Spoto press: for lockout work and starting power.
Tempo reps: more control of the eccentric and more starting power.
Wide grip: more chest-emphasized starting power.
Close grip: more triceps-emphasized starting power.
Overhead press: stability during the lift.
Incline dumbbell press: more chest starting power.

sections.heading: Squat
body: Adductor/abductor machines: stability during the lift, and they prevent the knees from collapsing.
Front squats: more stabilization and improvement in quadriceps power.
Box squats: more quadriceps starting power.
RDL: more hip extension and posterior chain strength.
Hip thrusts: increase hip extension strength.

sections.heading: Deadlift
body: RDL: more hip extension and posterior chain strength.
Hip thrusts: increase hip extension strength.
Back extensions: more posterior chain strength and stability.
Reverse hypers: more posterior chain strength and stability.
Rowing: increases posterior chain strength and grip strength.

sections.heading: Bodybuilding options that pair with the programs
body: Choose your own favorite isolations, or use the muscle-by-muscle lists in the Aesthetics Program Guide. The power-building plan also lists these additional options.
Mid chest: machine-supported press, hand-elevated push-up. Lower chest: cable flyes, lower-chest focused.
Rowing (thickness): lever bent-over row.
Front delt: lying incline-bench front raise. Rear delt: overhead press behind the back.
